findings.summary: PostParse calls f.Set directly, bypassing setMultiValueParsingConfig, so env-var and file sources ignore the custom slice/map separators (regression from the previous global setup).
PreParse re-creates f.value, discarding the injected separator config (nil value for unapplied flags, old value for Local flags), so the first --flag value is split with default separators.
Separator config is read from the parsing command rather than the root or nearest ancestor, so subcommands and inherited persistent flags fall back to default separators (behavior regression).
disableSliceFlagSeparator changed from var to const and is always false, leaving dead state that flag_test.go:3094 still passes as an argument.
New tests do not cover env or file sources, Local flags, or subcommands, so the regressions are not caught.
